examples.en: They found a gold vein in the mountains.
I heard there is a large mineral vein in this area.
A mineral vein runs long underground.
Copper came out of the new vein.

examples.ko: 광맥까지 파 내려가는 데 몇 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took months to dig down to the vein.
People wandered the mountains looking for a vein of ore.

explain: 광석이 줄기처럼 길게 모여 묻혀 있는 곳을 말해요. '금광맥', '철광맥'처럼 앞에 광물 이름을 붙여 쓰기도 해요. 보통 '광맥을 찾다', '광맥을 발견하다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 그들은 몇 년 동안 광맥을 찾았어요.
phrases.en: They searched for a mineral vein for years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 광석이 묻힌 곳을 찾아다닐 때 가장 흔하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for looking for where ore is buried.
phrases.en_equiv: to look for a mineral vein

phrases.en: An iron vein was found in this mountain.
phrases.nuance_ko: '광맥' 앞에 광물 이름을 붙이면 어떤 광석인지 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Putting a mineral name before 'gwangmaek' tells which ore it is.

phrases.en: They dug a tunnel underground along the vein.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄기처럼 이어진 광맥의 모양을 살려서 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the stream-like shape of a vein: following it as it runs.

explain_en: It is a place where ore lies buried in a long, stream-like line. You can put a mineral name before it, as in '금광맥' (gold vein) and '철광맥' (iron vein). The usual patterns are '광맥을 찾다' and '광맥을 발견하다'.

en: to be recorded; to be written down; to be logged

examples.ko: 이 대회 결과는 역사에 기록될 거예요.
examples.en: This tournament's result will go down in history.
Every conversation is recorded on the computer.
The highest temperature was recorded that day.
The recorded time isn't accurate.
His name is recorded in the book.

examples.ko: 내 이름이 명단에 기록되는 순간을 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw the moment my name was recorded on the list.

explain: '기록되다'는 어떤 내용이 글이나 자료로 남는다는 뜻이에요. '적히다'는 글자로 쓰여 있다는 쪽이고, '기록되다'는 나중에 참고하려고 남겨 둔다는 느낌이 강해요. '신기록이 기록되다'처럼 같은 말이 겹치면 '신기록을 세우다'가 자연스러워요. 능동형은 '기록하다'예요.

phrases.en: What happened that day was kept on record.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나중에 볼 수 있게 자료로 남을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something remains as a record to look at later.

phrases.en: All the visit times are recorded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 남겨진 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the state of already being recorded.

phrases.en: My name is written on the list.
phrases.nuance_ko: '기록되다'보다 글자로 쓰여 있다는 느낌이 강해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Has a stronger sense of simply being written in letters than 기록되다.

explain_en: '기록되다' means content is kept as writing or data. '적히다' just means being written down, while '기록되다' feels like being kept for later reference. If the word repeats, as in '신기록이 기록되다', '신기록을 세우다' sounds more natural. The active form is '기록하다'.

dis.h: be written down or logged on record

p.n: With 녹음되다 the lesson is audio-recorded; with 기록되다 it is logged or noted down.

examples.en: Lead is a heavy, soft metal.

examples.ko: 오래된 수도관에서 납이 나올 수 있어요.
examples.en: Lead can leach from old water pipes.

examples.ko: 이 페인트에는 납이 들어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: This paint contains no lead.

examples.ko: 납으로 만든 낚시 추가 바닥에 가라앉았어요.
examples.en: The fishing weight made of lead sank to the bottom.

examples.ko: 납 성분 때문에 이 제품은 판매가 중지됐어요.
examples.en: Sales of this product were stopped because of its lead content.
I saw news that lead was detected in a toy.

explain: '세금을 납부하다'의 '납'과 소리가 같아서 문장 속 맥락으로 구분해요. 금속 '납'은 주로 납 중독, 수도관, 페인트처럼 건강과 안전 뉴스에 나와요. 무거운 금속이라 낚시 추, 배터리에도 써요.

phrases.example: 오래된 페인트 때문에 납 중독이 생길 수 있어요.
phrases.en: Old paint can cause lead poisoning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 납이 몸에 쌓여 생기는 병이에요. 건강 뉴스에서 가장 자주 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An illness caused by lead building up in the body, the most frequent pairing in health news.

phrases.example: 이 물에서는 납 성분이 나오지 않았어요.
phrases.en: No lead was found in this water.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이나 제품 속에 납이 들어 있는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about whether lead is contained in water or a product.

phrases.example: 옛날 낚시 추는 납으로 만든 것이 많아요.
phrases.en: Many old fishing weights are made of lead.
phrases.nuance_ko: 재료가 납이라는 것을 말할 때 쓰는 활용형이에요. 무거운 금속이라는 성질과 이어져요.
phrases.nuance_en: A form used to say the material is lead, linked to its nature as a heavy metal.

explain_en: It sounds the same as the '납' in '납부하다' (pay a tax), so context tells them apart. The metal '납' mostly appears in health and safety news: lead poisoning, pipes, paint. It is heavy, so it is also used in fishing weights and batteries.

examples.en: An apple falls because of universal gravitation.
Newton discovered the law of universal gravitation.
The greater an object's mass, the greater the gravitational force.

examples.ko: 달이 지구 주위를 도는 것도 만유인력 덕분이에요.
examples.en: The moon orbiting the Earth is also thanks to universal gravitation.
We learned about universal gravitation in science class.

examples.ko: 만유인력이 없다면 우리는 땅에 서 있을 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without gravitation, we couldn't stand on the ground.

explain: 과학 시간에 '만유인력의 법칙'으로 많이 나오는 말이에요. 일상에서 땅이 끌어당기는 힘을 말할 때는 '중력'이 더 자주 쓰여요. 만유인력은 모든 물체 사이에 작용하는 힘이라는 점이 달라요.

phrases.en: Newton discovered the law of universal gravitation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 시간에 가장 자주 나오는 덩어리예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The chunk you'll hear most in science class.

phrases.example: 달이 지구 주위를 도는 것은 만유인력 때문이에요.
phrases.en: The moon goes around the Earth because of universal gravitation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원인을 설명할 때 '때문에'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 때문에 to explain a cause.

phrases.en: Gravity is weaker on the moon.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 땅이 끌어당기는 힘은 '중력'이라고 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In daily life, the pull of the ground is called 중력.

explain_en: It mostly appears in science class as '만유인력의 법칙'. In daily life, for the pull of the ground, '중력' is used more often. The difference is that 만유인력 refers to the force acting between all objects.

examples.en: The source of the Han River is in Taebaek, Gangwon Province.

examples.ko: 이 강의 발원지를 찾아 산을 올랐어요.
examples.en: I climbed the mountain to find the source of this river.
The closer to the source, the clearer the water.
They say there is a small spring at the source.
The source of the Nakdong River is also in Taebaek.

examples.ko: 이 병의 발원지가 어디인지 아직 밝혀지지 않았어요.
examples.en: Where this disease originated has not been found out yet.

explain: 강이 처음 시작되는 곳을 말해요. 병이나 유행이 시작된 곳에 비유해서 쓰기도 해요. 문화나 운동이 시작된 곳은 보통 '발상지'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The source of the Nakdong River is in Taebaek City.
phrases.nuance_ko: '강 이름 + 의'를 붙여 강이 시작되는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add a river name plus 의 to name where the river begins.

phrases.en: This river flows 300 kilometers from its source to the sea.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강의 시작과 끝을 함께 말할 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An expression used to describe a river's start and end together.
phrases.en_equiv: from the source to the sea

phrases.en: I heard that village was the origin of the epidemic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 병이나 유행이 처음 시작된 곳을 비유할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used figuratively for where an illness or trend first started.
phrases.en_equiv: origin of an outbreak or trend

explain_en: It is the place where a river begins. It is also used figuratively for where a disease or trend started. The place where a culture or movement began is usually called '발상지'.

examples.en: Korea is in the Northern Hemisphere.
When it is summer in the Northern Hemisphere, it is winter in the Southern Hemisphere.

examples.ko: 북반구에서는 칠월이 가장 더운 달 중 하나예요.
examples.en: In the Northern Hemisphere, July is one of the hottest months.

examples.ko: 이 철새는 가을마다 북반구에서 남쪽으로 이동해요.
examples.en: This migratory bird moves south from the Northern Hemisphere every autumn.
The Northern and Southern Hemispheres have opposite seasons.
We are in the Northern Hemisphere, so Christmas is in winter.

explain: 적도를 기준으로 북쪽 절반을 말하고 반대말은 '남반구'예요. 한국, 미국, 유럽이 북반구에 있어요. 북반구가 여름이면 남반구는 겨울이라서 호주에서는 크리스마스가 한여름이에요.

phrases.en: Australia is in the Southern Hemisphere.
phrases.nuance_ko: '북반구'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 북반구.

phrases.en: Korea is in the Northern Hemisphere, so December is winter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 도시가 어디에 있는지 말할 때 '에 있다'를 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 에 있다 to say where a country or city is located.
phrases.en_equiv: to be in the Northern Hemisphere

phrases.en: The seasons are opposite in the Northern and Southern Hemispheres.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 지역을 비교할 때 같이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said together when comparing the two regions.

explain_en: It means the northern half of the Earth, divided at the equator, and its opposite is '남반구'. Korea, the United States and Europe are all in the Northern Hemisphere. When it is summer in the north it is winter in the south, so Christmas falls in midsummer in Australia.

examples.ko: 이 약을 쓰면 해로운 세균이 사멸해요.
examples.en: If you use this medicine, the harmful bacteria die off.

examples.ko: 열을 가하면 세균이 사멸한다고 과학 시간에 배웠어요.
examples.en: I learned in science class that bacteria die when heat is applied.

examples.ko: 환경이 바뀌면서 그 식물은 서서히 사멸하고 있어요.
examples.en: As the environment changed, that plant has been slowly dying out.

examples.ko: 사멸한 줄 알았던 동물이 다시 발견되었어요.
examples.en: An animal thought to be extinct was found again.

examples.ko: 물이 오염되면 작은 생물들이 사멸할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If water gets polluted, small organisms can die out.

examples.ko: 소독하지 않으면 세균이 사멸하지 않을 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you don't disinfect, the bacteria may not be destroyed.

explain: 세균, 식물, 동물, 문명처럼 완전히 없어지는 것에 써요. 사람이 죽는 것에는 쓰지 않고 '죽다', '돌아가시다'를 써요. 종 전체가 없어질 때는 '멸종하다'도 쓰고, '사멸'은 과학 글에서 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.en: This disinfectant kills bacteria.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사멸하다'에 '시키다'를 붙여 어떤 것을 완전히 없애는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '시키다' makes it mean to cause something to die out completely.

phrases.example: 환경이 나빠져서 많은 생물이 사멸해 가고 있어요.
phrases.en: Many living things are dying out as the environment worsens.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-아/어 가다'로 서서히 없어지는 과정을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-아/어 가다' shows a gradual process of dying out.

phrases.en: Dinosaurs went extinct long ago.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물 종 전체가 없어질 때 '사멸하다'보다 더 널리 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: More commonly used than '사멸하다' when a whole animal species disappears.

explain_en: It is used for things that disappear completely, such as bacteria, plants, animals and civilizations. It is not used for a person's death; for that, use '죽다' or '돌아가시다'. When a whole species disappears, '멸종하다' is also used, and '사멸' shows up in science writing.

examples.en: The coral reef under the sea is really beautiful.
Small fish swim among the coral reef.
The seawater is getting warmer, so the coral reefs are dying.

examples.ko: 이번 여행에서 산호초를 보러 스노클링을 했어요.
examples.en: On this trip I went snorkeling to see the coral reef.

examples.ko: 호주에는 세계에서 가장 큰 산호초가 있어요.
examples.en: Australia has the biggest coral reef in the world.
Be careful not to step on the coral reef.

explain: 산호초는 산호가 모여서 만든 바위 같은 지형이에요. 산호 하나하나는 '산호'라고 하고, 여러 개가 쌓인 큰 덩어리는 산호초라고 해요. 환경 뉴스에서 '산호초 백화 현상'처럼 자주 들어요.

phrases.en: Corals come in many colors.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산호'는 하나하나를, '산호초'는 모여서 된 큰 지형을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '산호' is each coral; '산호초' is the large formation they make.

phrases.example: 바다를 깨끗이 해서 산호초를 보호해야 해요.
phrases.en: We must keep the sea clean to protect the coral reefs.
phrases.nuance_ko: 환경을 지키자는 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about protecting the environment.

phrases.example: 바닷물이 뜨거워지면 산호초 백화 현상이 생겨요.
phrases.en: When seawater gets hot, coral bleaching happens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산호초가 하얗게 변하는 환경 문제를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the environmental problem of reefs turning white.

explain_en: 산호초 is a rock-like formation built up by corals. A single piece is '산호', and the large mass they build is 산호초. In environmental news you often hear '산호초 백화 현상' (coral bleaching).

examples.ko: 매미는 땅속에서 오래 지내다가 성충이 돼요.
examples.en: Cicadas spend a long time underground before becoming adults.
A larva grows into an adult insect through the pupa stage.

examples.ko: 성충은 날개가 있어서 멀리 날 수 있어요.
examples.en: Adult insects have wings, so they can fly far.
I researched the environment adult insects need.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 나비의 성충과 애벌레를 비교했어요.
examples.en: In science class we compared the adult butterfly and the caterpillar.
I saw many adult dragonflies by the pond.

explain: 곤충이 다 자란 모습을 말하고, 반대말은 '유충'이나 '애벌레'예요. 사람이나 동물에는 쓰지 않고 곤충 이야기에서만 써요.

phrases.en: When a dragonfly becomes an adult, it flies in the sky.
phrases.nuance_ko: 곤충이 다 자라는 순간을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for the moment an insect finishes growing up.

phrases.en: A butterfly grows from a caterpillar into an adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 변화의 과정을 보여 줄 때 '-에서 -으로'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'from ~ to ~' to show the process of change.
phrases.en_equiv: to grow into an adult insect

phrases.en: A larva looks different from an adult.
phrases.nuance_ko: 성충의 반대말로, 어린 곤충을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 성충, referring to a young insect.

explain_en: It refers to an insect in its fully grown form, and its opposite is '유충' or '애벌레'. It is not used for people or other animals, only in talk about insects.

examples.ko: 이 집은 수맥 위에 있어서 잠이 안 온대요.
examples.en: They say this house sits on a water vein, so you can't sleep.

examples.ko: 우물을 팔 곳을 정하려고 수맥부터 알아봐요.
examples.en: To decide where to dig a well, we check the water vein first.

examples.ko: 땅속 수맥이 막혀서 물이 안 나와요.
examples.en: The underground water vein is blocked, so no water comes out.
I called an expert who surveys water veins.

examples.ko: 수맥으로 물이 흘러서 땅이 늘 촉촉해요.
examples.en: Water flows through the vein, so the ground is always damp.
I moved the bed far away from the water vein.

explain: 땅속에서 물이 흐르는 줄기를 말하고, 우물을 팔 때 중요해요. 민간에서는 집터나 잠자리에 수맥이 있으면 좋지 않다는 이야기도 하지만, 일반적인 말은 '지하수'예요.

phrases.en: We looked for a water vein before digging a well.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우물이나 집터 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Common when talking about wells or building sites.

phrases.example: 이 땅 밑에는 수맥이 흐르고 있어요.
phrases.en: A water vein runs beneath this land.
phrases.nuance_ko: 물이 땅속에서 흐르는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes water flowing underground.

phrases.en: This village drinks groundwater.
phrases.nuance_ko: '수맥'은 물줄기이고 '지하수'는 땅속의 물 자체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: 수맥 is the water's channel; 지하수 is the water itself.

explain_en: It is a stream of water flowing underground, important when digging a well. Folk belief also says a water vein under a house or bed is bad, but the general word for groundwater is '지하수'.

examples.en: In the Cenozoic era, mammals increased greatly.
Dinosaurs lived in the Mesozoic, not the Cenozoic.
Cenozoic fossils were found in this area.
The Cenozoic is an era that continues to the present.
The Paleozoic, Mesozoic and Cenozoic eras came up on the exam.
There was an ice age in the late Cenozoic.

explain: 지구의 역사를 나눈 '고생대, 중생대, 신생대' 중 마지막 시대로, 이 세 개를 한 묶음으로 외우는 경우가 많아요. 공룡은 중생대 이야기라서 헷갈리지 않게 조심하세요.

phrases.en: I saw Cenozoic fossils at the museum.
phrases.nuance_ko: 박물관이나 과학 수업에서 시대를 붙여 화석을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in museums and science class to name fossils by era.

phrases.en: The Cenozoic comes after the Mesozoic.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지질 시대의 순서를 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to explain the order of geological eras.

phrases.en: Mammoths are among the Cenozoic animals.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 시대에 살았던 생물을 말할 때 '신생대'를 앞에 붙여요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put 신생대 in front to talk about creatures that lived in that era.

explain_en: It is the last of the three eras '고생대, 중생대, 신생대' in Earth's history, and people usually memorize them as a set. Dinosaurs belong to the Mesozoic, so be careful not to mix them up.

examples.en: Almost no sunlight reaches the deep sea.
Deep-sea fish have unusual shapes.
Scientists found a new creature in the deep sea.

examples.ko: 심해는 압력이 높아서 사람이 가기 어려워요.
examples.en: The pressure is high in the deep sea, so it is hard for people to go.
A submersible went down to the deep sea and took photos.

examples.ko: 저는 심해를 다룬 다큐멘터리를 자주 봐요.
examples.en: I often watch documentaries about the deep sea.

explain: '심해 생물', '심해어', '심해 탐사'처럼 뒤에 명사를 붙여 쓰는 일이 많아요. 일상 대화에서는 '깊은 바다'라고 말해도 돼요. 과학 기사나 다큐멘터리에서는 심해라고 해요.

phrases.example: 심해어는 눈이 아주 크거나 모양이 특이해요.
phrases.en: Deep-sea fish have very big eyes or unusual shapes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심해'에 사는 물고기를 한 단어로 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A single word for fish that live in the deep sea.

phrases.en: Scientists set out on a deep-sea expedition.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 다큐멘터리에서 바다 깊은 곳을 조사할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in news and documentaries for exploring the deep ocean.

phrases.example: 깊은 바다에는 빛이 잘 들어오지 않아요.
phrases.en: Light hardly reaches the deep ocean.
phrases.nuance_ko: '심해'와 뜻이 같지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 심해, but more casual and used in everyday talk.

explain_en: It often takes a noun after it, as in '심해 생물', '심해어' (deep-sea fish), and '심해 탐사' (deep-sea exploration). In everyday talk you can say '깊은 바다' instead. Science articles and documentaries use 심해.

examples.ko: 이 산은 단단한 암석으로 이루어져 있어요.
examples.en: This mountain is made of hard rock.

examples.ko: 박물관에서 여러 가지 암석을 직접 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can see various kinds of rock in person at the museum.

examples.ko: 바람과 물에 오랫동안 깎인 암석이 신기한 모양이 되었어요.
examples.en: The rock, worn away by wind and water for a long time, took on an amazing shape.

examples.ko: 암석 표본을 교실에 가져와서 친구들에게 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: I brought a rock sample to class and showed it to my classmates.

examples.ko: 이 지역의 암석과 흙은 색이 서로 달라요.
examples.en: The rock and soil in this area are different in color.

examples.ko: 이 암석에서 작은 물고기 화석이 발견됐어요.
examples.en: A small fish fossil was found in this rock.

explain: '돌'은 일상에서 두루 쓰고 '바위'는 크고 단단한 덩어리를 말해요. '암석'은 과학이나 지리 수업, 설명하는 글에서 주로 써요. '화성암', '퇴적암'처럼 종류 이름에는 '암'이 들어가요.

phrases.example: 과학실에서 여러 가지 암석 표본을 봤어요.
phrases.en: In the science room, I saw several kinds of rock specimens.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수업이나 연구에서 보여 주려고 모아 둔 암석을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: This refers to rocks collected to show in class or research.

phrases.en: The scholars collected rocks from the mountain and examined them.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조사나 연구를 위해 암석을 가져올 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a formal phrase for taking rocks for research or investigation.

phrases.en: I sat on a boulder and rested for a moment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '암석'보다 일상적이고, 크고 단단한 덩어리를 가리킬 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It is more everyday than 암석 and refers to a big, hard mass of rock.

explain_en: '돌' is the everyday word and '바위' means a big hard mass. '암석' is mostly used in science or geography classes and in explanatory writing. Names of rock types contain '암', as in '화성암' (igneous rock) and '퇴적암' (sedimentary rock).

examples.en: Squid and clams are mollusks.
We learned the features of mollusks in science class.
Snails also belong to the mollusks.
Mollusks have no bones and soft bodies.

examples.ko: 시험에 연체동물과 절지동물을 구별하는 문제가 나왔어요.
examples.en: The test had a question on telling mollusks from arthropods.

examples.ko: 연체동물 중에는 껍데기가 있는 것도 있고 없는 것도 있어요.
examples.en: Among mollusks, some have shells and some don't.

explain: 학교 과학 수업에서 쓰는 분류 이름이에요. 일상 대화에서는 오징어, 조개, 달팽이처럼 구체적인 이름으로 말해요. 같은 계열의 분류 이름으로 '절지동물', '척추동물'도 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: Octopuses are also among the types of mollusks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 동물이 연체동물에 들어가는지 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when explaining which animals count as mollusks.

phrases.en: Snails also belong to the mollusks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동물이 어느 분류에 들어가는지 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used to say which category an animal belongs to.

phrases.en: How are mollusks and arthropods different?
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 분류와 비교해서 공부할 때 함께 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Appears together when comparing with another animal group in study.

explain_en: It is a classification name used in school science. In daily talk people name the animals themselves, such as squid, clams or snails. Related classification terms worth knowing are '절지동물' and '척추동물'.

examples.en: Soil contains a lot of organic matter.
When fallen leaves rot, they become organic matter.
If there is a lot of organic matter in water, it smells.
Plants make organic matter by themselves.
Compost is a fertilizer made from organic matter.
In science class we learned organic and inorganic matter.

explain: 과학 시간에 '유기물'과 '무기물'을 짝으로 배워요. 생물에서 나오거나 탄소가 들어 있는 물질이 유기물이에요. 식품에서 말하는 '유기농'과 글자는 비슷해도 쓰임은 달라요.

phrases.en: This soil is rich in organic matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흙이나 물에 유기물이 많이 들어 있다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that soil or water contains a lot of organic matter.

phrases.en: We learned about organic and inorganic matter in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유기물과 반대되는 무기물을 짝으로 묶어 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pairs organic matter with its opposite, inorganic matter.

phrases.en: Insects and tiny organisms break down organic matter.
phrases.nuance_ko: 썩는 과정을 설명할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common collocation when explaining how things decompose.

explain_en: In science class it is learned as a pair, 유기물 and 무기물. Organic matter comes from living things or contains carbon. It looks like 유기농 (organic farming) in food talk, but they are used differently.

examples.en: Our solar system is inside the galaxy.

examples.ko: 어릴 때부터 은하계에 관한 책을 즐겨 읽었어요.
examples.en: Since I was little, I have enjoyed reading books about galaxies.

examples.ko: 영화 속 주인공이 은하계를 여행하며 모험을 해요.
examples.en: The hero of the movie travels the galaxy and has adventures.
They say there are hundreds of billions of stars in the galaxy.
I tried taking a picture of the galaxy with a telescope.

examples.ko: 우리 은하계 밖에는 또 다른 은하들이 있어요.
examples.en: Outside our galaxy there are other galaxies.

explain: 과학 수업에서는 '은하'라고 짧게 말하는 일이 많아요. '은하수'는 밤하늘에 길게 보이는 별의 띠를 말할 때 써서 '은하계'와 달라요. 영화나 만화에서는 '은하계를 지키다'처럼 크고 멋있는 느낌으로 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: I learned about galaxies in science class.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은하계'를 짧게 줄인 말로, 수업이나 과학 글에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 은하계, used more often in science classes and writing.

phrases.example: 은하계 밖에는 또 다른 은하가 아주 많아요.
phrases.en: Outside our galaxy, there are many other galaxies.
phrases.nuance_ko: '은하계'가 우리가 사는 곳의 범위를 나타낼 때 '밖'과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 밖 to talk about the space beyond our own galaxy.

phrases.en: The hero in the movie protects the galaxy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 영화나 만화에서 크고 멋있는 느낌을 줄 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase in movies and comics that gives a grand, heroic feel.

explain_en: In science class people often say just '은하'. '은하수' is used for the band of stars you see across the night sky, so it differs from '은하계'. In movies and comics it appears with a grand feeling, as in '은하계를 지키다'.

examples.en: Bats find their way using sound waves.
Sound waves travel far even underwater.

examples.ko: 이 기계는 음파로 물고기 떼를 찾아내요.
examples.en: This machine finds schools of fish using sound waves.

examples.ko: 소리는 음파가 되어 공기를 타고 전달돼요.
examples.en: Sound becomes sound waves and travels through the air.

examples.ko: 음파의 진동이 약해서 소리가 잘 안 들려요.
examples.en: The vibration of the sound waves is weak, so I can't hear well.

examples.ko: 과학 시간에 음파를 그림으로 그려 봤어요.
examples.en: In science class we drew sound waves as pictures.

explain: 소리가 퍼져 나가는 파동을 말해서 과학 수업이나 설명에서 많이 나와요. 사람이 못 듣는 높은 소리는 '초음파'라고 하고, 병원 검사에서도 들을 수 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '소리'라고 해요.

phrases.en: I had an ultrasound exam at the hospital.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 못 듣는 높은 음파를 말하고, 병원 검사 이야기에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is a high-frequency sound wave that people can't hear. It often comes up in talk about hospital exams.

phrases.en: Bats send out sound waves to find food.
phrases.nuance_ko: '음파'와 함께 가장 자주 쓰는 동사 짝말로, 소리를 내보낸다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common verb pairing with 음파, meaning to emit a sound wave.

phrases.en: Sound waves spread in all directions through the air.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과학 설명에서 소리가 멀리 가는 모습을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in science explanations to describe sound traveling outward.

explain_en: It means the wave by which sound spreads, so it comes up mostly in science classes and explanations. Sound too high for people to hear is called '초음파' (ultrasound), which you also hear about in hospital exams. In everyday talk people simply say '소리'.

examples.ko: 햇빛이 지표면을 데우면 공기가 위로 올라가요.
examples.en: When sunlight heats the ground surface, the air rises.
The temperature of the ground surface is much higher than usual.

examples.ko: 이 지역은 지표면 아래에 물이 많이 흐른다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a lot of water flows beneath the ground surface in this area.
An earthquake struck and the ground surface cracked in many places.
The amount of ultraviolet light reaching the ground surface has increased.

examples.ko: 눈이 오자 하얗게 덮인 지표면이 눈부셨어요.
examples.en: After it snowed, the white-covered ground surface was dazzling.

explain: 땅의 겉면을 과학이나 지리 설명에서 말할 때 써요. 일상에서는 '땅바닥', '땅 표면'이라고 하고, '지면'도 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: When sunlight reaches the ground surface, the ground gets warm.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빛이나 열이 땅의 겉면에 이르는 것을 과학적으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A scientific way to say light or heat reaches the ground's surface.

phrases.en: In summer, the ground surface temperature rises a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 땅 겉면의 온도를 말할 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the temperature of the ground surface.

phrases.example: 비가 오면 땅 표면이 금방 젖어요.
phrases.en: When it rains, the surface of the ground gets wet quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '지표면'과 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 더 쉽게 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 지표면 but easier and more common in daily talk.

explain_en: It is used in science or geography explanations for the outer surface of the land. In daily life people say '땅바닥' or '땅 표면', and '지면' is used in a similar way.

en: to be collected; to be gathered

examples.en: They are examining the fingerprints collected at the scene.
This salt is gathered from clean seawater.

examples.ko: 약초는 아침 일찍 채취되는 것이 좋대요.
examples.en: I hear herbs are best gathered early in the morning.
Once the sample is collected, it is sent to the hospital right away.

examples.ko: 이 버섯은 가을 산에서 많이 채취됐어요.
examples.en: A lot of these mushrooms were gathered in the autumn mountains.

examples.ko: 채취되지 않은 열매는 그냥 땅에 떨어졌어요.
examples.en: The fruit that was not picked just fell to the ground.

explain: 채취되다는 '채취하다'의 결과를 말할 때 써요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 지문·샘플·약초 같은 물건이에요. 일상에서는 '따다', '캐다', '뽑다' 같은 말이 더 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: The collected samples are sent to the lab.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 모은 것을 꾸며 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe something that has already been collected.

phrases.en: The fingerprints haven't been collected yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 모으지 못했다는 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form: not yet collected.

phrases.en: The amount of this herb that is gathered is small.
phrases.nuance_ko: 얼마나 모이는지 양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about how much is gathered.

explain_en: 채취되다 reports the outcome of 채취하다, and the subject is a thing such as a fingerprint, sample or herb, not a person. In daily talk, verbs like '따다', '캐다' and '뽑다' are more common.

examples.ko: 강이 바다와 만나는 하구에는 새가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many birds at the river mouth where the river meets the sea.
I watched migratory birds at the mouth of the Nakdong River.
Near the river mouth, fresh water and sea water mix.

examples.ko: 이 하구는 갯벌이 넓어서 조개도 많이 잡혀요.
examples.en: This river mouth has wide mudflats, so lots of clams are caught.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 오면 하구로 흙탕물이 밀려와요.
examples.en: When it rains a lot, muddy water rushes toward the river mouth.

examples.ko: 강의 하구에 둑을 쌓은 곳도 있어요.
examples.en: In some places, a dam has been built at the river mouth.

explain: '강 하구'처럼 강이 바다로 들어가는 끝부분을 말해요. 강의 위쪽은 '상류', 아래쪽은 '하류'라고 해서 함께 알아 두면 좋아요. 지리 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.example: 강 하구에는 갯벌이 넓게 펼쳐져 있어요.
phrases.en: A wide tidal flat stretches out at the river mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: '하구'만 말해도 되지만 '강 하구'라고 하면 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can say just 하구, but 강 하구 makes it clearer.

phrases.en: I went fishing near the river mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 위치를 말할 때 '근처'와 함께 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often paired with 근처 to give a location.

phrases.en: I walked along the river toward the river mouth.
phrases.nuance_ko: 강의 아래쪽, 바다와 만나는 방향을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to indicate the downstream direction where the river meets the sea.

explain_en: It refers to the end of a river where it flows into the sea, as in '강 하구'. The upper part of a river is '상류' and the lower part is '하류', so learn them together. You often see it in geography lessons and the news.
